annotations.title: Assess AI initiative from plain English

description: The front door for one AI investment decision. CALL THIS FIRST when the user describes an AI idea in ordinary language or asks whether it should proceed. It works as a short guided conversation and returns one thing to ask at a time. Pass the proposal unchanged on every call, plus everything the user has answered so far. needs_input: a piece of context (industry, business function, AI type or headcount) could not be read; ask question and pass the answer in its named field. needs_confirmation: show the understood statement, ask the user whether it is right, then call again with confirmed true or with the corrected item. not_enough_to_judge: ask question, the next of at most five plain questions, showing every choice label; pass the id of the choice the user picks in answers. When question is absent, tell the user what is listed in to_find_out and stop. verdict: Accelerate, Fix or Stop, resting only on the user's answers. Give the user summary first, then each item in holding_back with what they said and what it needs to become, then first_step; these are written in everyday words, so do not replace them with framework terms. Lead with warning whenever it is present. This tool fills in no score and returns no euro figure, so never state a euro benefit from this result, never set confirmed and never pick an answer on behalf of the user; when the user is unsure, pass unknown. Organisations under 250 people get questions worded for a smaller firm, with the same rules for every size. Use score_initiative when canonical fields and 0 to 100 scores are already known and a planning range is wanted for advisory work, score_portfolio for several initiatives, and diagnose_process for measured waste in a running process. Deterministic calculation with no authentication. Anonymous usage telemetry may be sent; set AIBVF_TELEMETRY_DISABLE=1 to opt out.

ai_tier.description: Answer or correction: automation/RPA, GenAI/copilot, or agentic/autonomous. Overrides anything read from proposal.

answers.description: The user's answers to the guided questions, by question id. Each value is the id of the choice the user picked: a, b, c, d, or unknown when the user does not know yet. Pass every answer given so far on each call. Never pick an answer on behalf of the user.

confirmed.description: Set true only after the user has seen the understood statement and said it is right. Never set it on behalf of the user.

employees.description: Number of people in the organisation. Under 250 the questions are worded for a smaller firm; the rules are the same for every size.

function.description: Answer or correction in canonical or everyday language, for example customer service, procurement, finance or risk. Overrides anything read from proposal.

industry.description: Answer or correction in canonical or everyday language, for example retail, hospital, bank or public sector. Overrides anything read from proposal.

proposal.description: The AI initiative in the user's own words. Pass it unchanged on every call. The tool reads industry, business function, AI type and headcount from it and never guesses an unread value.

readiness.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored. The front door verdict does not use the operating-model label.

revenue_eur.description: Accepted for compatibility and ignored. The front door verdict does not use revenue.

scores.description: OPTIONAL, for callers that already hold 0 to 100 pillar scores from the user. A regular user answers the guided questions and never needs this. A supplied score takes precedence over an answer. Never invent a number: this tool fills in nothing.

change_enablement.description: Optional; when omitted, estimated from readiness (agile 55, traditional 45, siloed 32 — always below the 60 floor, because an unevidenced change capability is unproven). Sponsor in place, owner named, change budget funded (0–100, higher is better). Must be ≥ 60 for an Accelerate verdict.

financial_return.description: Optional; when omitted, estimated from the disclosed AI BVF planning range for the function (40–52, never enough to clear 60 unmodelled, never low enough to force a Stop). Strength of the modelled return (0–100, higher is better). A value ≤ 20 forces a Stop on its own; ≥ 60 is one of the four conditions required for Accelerate.

governance_risk.description: Optional; when omitted, estimated from tier and regulated context (gen1 30 / gen2 42 / gen3 55, +10 in a regulated function, +8 in a regulated industry — agentic AI in regulated finance estimates at 73 and forces a Stop until governance evidence exists). This pillar is INVERTED: higher means MORE risk. ≥ 70 forces a Stop on its own; must be ≤ 40 for Accelerate.

strategic_alignment.description: Optional; estimated at 50 (unproven) when omitted, since alignment to a board KPI cannot be read from context. How clearly this moves a board-level KPI (0–100, higher is better). Must be ≥ 60 — together with financial_return ≥ 60, change_enablement ≥ 60 and governance_risk ≤ 40 — for an Accelerate verdict.

signal_completeness.description: Optional 0 to 1 input-quality factor. The default ranges from 0.5 when all pillars are estimated to 1 when all are supplied. Supplied values still require evidence review. Lower this factor when the supplied pillars rest on weak evidence.

work_architecture.description: Evidence that workflows, roles, decision rights and measures are ready. Pass only what is known. Explicit gaps and omitted checks block Accelerate until all four checks are evidenced.

decision_rights_defined.description: True only when decision, override and escalation rights have named human owners, false when authority remains unclear.

measures_updated.description: True only when performance measures and incentives reflect the redesigned work, false when the old measures remain.

roles_redesigned.description: True only when affected roles, accountabilities and capability expectations have been rewritten, false when roles remain unchanged.

workflow_redesigned.description: True only when the end-to-end workflow has been redesigned around the AI and retained human judgement, false when the existing workflow remains.

name: assess_ai_initiative

also_open.description: not_enough_to_judge only. Anything still open after the three in decides.

ambiguous_fields.description: Fields whose wording pointed to more than one value, each with the competing values. Ask the user to choose; never choose for them.

decides.description: not_enough_to_judge only. Up to three things still to answer, most decisive first.

answer_in.description: The input field that carries the answer on the next call.

inferred_fields.description: Fields read from the wording of the proposal instead of an explicit answer.

next_question.description: The one thing to ask the user next, as a sentence. Absent when status is verdict.

proposal.description: The supplied proposal, returned so the next call can preserve it verbatim.

question.description: The same question in structured form. Show the question and every choice label to the user, in the given order, and pass back the id of the choice they pick in the field named by answer_in. Ask one question per turn.

number.description: Guided questions only: position in the sequence.

why.description: Why the answer decides the outcome.

resolutions.description: Every deterministic resolution, naming the field, canonical value, source and matched phrase.

resolved_inputs.description: Context resolved so far: industry, function, ai_tier, employees and track (smaller_firm under 250 people, otherwise enterprise).

status.description: needs_input: a piece of context is unread, ask question. needs_confirmation: show understood and ask the user to confirm or correct it. not_enough_to_judge: ask question, the next guided question. verdict: Accelerate, Fix or Stop from the user's answers only.

suggestions.description: Accepted values for an explicitly supplied field that could not be resolved.

to_find_out.description: Questions the user answered with "I do not know yet". A verdict waits on these. When no question is left to ask, tell the user to find these out and come back.

answer_in.description: The input field that carries the answer on the next call.

understood.description: Plain statement of how the proposal was read. Show it to the user before anything else and invite corrections.

verdict.description: Present only when status is verdict. Rests only on what the user answered or supplied. Carries no euro figure and no estimated score.

advisory_next_step.description: Optional CTA, present only for Fix/Stop verdicts.

answers_given.description: The guided answers behind those scores: the choice, its wording and the published score it carries.

audit.description: Reproducibility record: engine version, the rules that fired, and the resolved inputs. Deterministic, no timestamps. If the verdict is challenged months later, the same inputs on the same engine version reproduce it exactly.

inputs_used.description: The resolved inputs the result was computed on, including estimated pillar values.

rules_fired.description: The rules that actually fired, in order: estimation, gates, classification, value arithmetic.

decision_confidence.description: Heuristic decision score, 0 to 100, with no probability calibration. Present only when all four pillars were supplied.

feedback.description: Optional three-question feedback route, present only for Fix/Stop verdicts. The page records the response anonymously only when the user chooses an answer; no assessment data is attached.

first_step.description: The one thing to do first. Give it after the summary.

holding_back.description: The answers that keep the initiative from a go-ahead, most decisive first. Empty for Accelerate. Show each with what the user said and what it needs to become.

needed.description: What the answer has to become to clear the bar.

short.description: A short name for the question, for lists.

interpretation.description: How to read decision_confidence. Present only when all four pillars were supplied.

reason.description: The rule that produced the classification, in framework terms. For audit and advisory use; prefer summary when speaking to the user.

scores_supplied.description: The pillar scores the verdict rests on, from answers or supplied scores. Nothing here was estimated.

summary.description: The outcome in one or two plain sentences. A Stop quotes its cause. Lead with this.

value_note.description: Why no euro figure is given.

verdict_flips.description: The nearest single-pillar movements that change the verdict. Present only when all four pillars were supplied.

work_architecture.description: The work architecture gate across workflow, roles, human decision rights and performance measures. A stated gap or missing evidence blocks Accelerate.

warning.description: A condition the user must meet first. Lead with it when present.
